## Comparability caveat

All five companies report on a calendar fiscal year (Jan 1 – Dec 31, 2024), so the periods align [DOC-1]. However, **Alaska Air Group's FY2024 figures are not fully comparable** to the other four: Alaska completed its acquisition of Hawaiian Holdings on September 18, 2024, and Hawaiian's results are consolidated only from that date forward, contributing $869 million of revenue (and a $113 million net loss) for the stub period [DOC-2]. Alaska's FY2024 ratios therefore blend ~8.5 months of standalone Alaska with ~3.5 months of a combined entity, and are not representative of a full-year combined cost structure.

## Aircraft fuel expense as % of revenue (lowest first)

| Rank | Airline | Fuel / Revenue | Calculation |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Delta | **17.1%** | $10,566M / $61,643M [DOC-1] |
| 2 | United | **20.6%** | $11,756M / $57,063M [DOC-1] |
| 3 | American | **21.1%** | $11,418M / $54,211M [DOC-1] |
| 4 | Southwest | **21.1%** | $5,812M / $27,483M [DOC-1] |
| 5 | Alaska | **21.4%** | $2,506M / $11,735M [DOC-1], [DOC-2] |

(American 21.06% vs. Southwest 21.15% — effectively a tie.)

## Salaries, wages and benefits as % of revenue (lowest first)

| Rank | Airline | Labor / Revenue | Calculation |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Delta | **26.2%** | $16,161M / $61,643M [DOC-1] |
| 2 | United | **29.2%** | $16,678M / $57,063M [DOC-1] |
| 3 | American | **29.6%** | $16,021M / $54,211M [DOC-1] |
| 4 | Alaska | **30.6%** | $3,588M / $11,735M [DOC-1], [DOC-2] |
| 5 | Southwest | **44.5%** | $12,240M / $27,483M [DOC-1] |

## Conclusion

Yes — **Delta ranks lowest (top-ranked) on both metrics**, at 17.1% fuel and 26.2% labor, consistent with its industry-leading revenue base of $61,643M and highest operating income of $5,995M [DOC-1]. Delta's fuel ratio is also aided by its refinery operations (not separately broken out here). The two rankings diverge most in the tail: Southwest is mid-pack on fuel (21.1%) but a clear outlier on labor intensity (44.5%), while Alaska is highest on fuel but only fourth on labor — though Alaska's position in both rankings should be treated cautiously given the partial-period Hawaiian consolidation [DOC-2].

ANSWER: Fuel % of revenue (lowest first): Delta 17.1%, United 20.6%, American 21.1%, Southwest 21.1%, Alaska 21.4%. Salaries/wages/benefits % of revenue (lowest first): Delta 26.2%, United 29.2%, American 29.6%, Alaska 30.6%, Southwest 44.5%. Yes — Delta is top-ranked (lowest) in both; note Alaska's ratios include Hawaiian only from Sept 18, 2024 and are not fully comparable.
